wu: Play 'Find Someone Who...' with quantifiers: students mingle asking 'Do you have plenty of energy?' and 'Do you hardly ever skip breakfast?', tallying responses on a worksheet.
wuAlt: Play 'Frequency Auction': students bid on statements like 'I tend to drink coffee every morning' using play money.
Play 'Lifestyle Bingo': students find peers who match habits like 'plenty of free time' and mark their cards.
pres: Show a photo of a busy professional and a relaxed freelancer, contrasting their routines with model sentences like 'He tends to work 12 hours a day' and 'She hardly ever checks emails after 6 PM'. Use flashcards for 'plenty of' and 'hardly any' to visualize quantity.
presAlt: Present a short video clip of two people discussing their daily habits, pausing to highlight target language.
Distribute a lifestyle survey with gaps for quantifiers, demonstrating how to complete it with 'tend to' and adverbs.
prac: Complete a 'Habit Comparison' worksheet with fill-in-the-blank sentences using present simple vs continuous and quantifiers, then peer-check answers. Play 'Sentence Auction' where students correct sentences with incorrect quantifiers.
pracAlt: Play 'Quantifier Swap': students rewrite sentences replacing 'plenty of' with 'hardly any' and vice versa.
Do 'Role-Drill Pairs': one student describes a habit, the other asks follow-up questions using target language.
ls: Listen to a podcast segment about work-life balance, noting down how often two professionals use quantifiers like 'plenty of' and 'hardly any' to describe their habits.
re: Play 'Quick Draw': students race to draw a habit (e.g., 'plenty of exercise') while others guess using target language.
prod: Roleplay a job interview where candidates discuss their work habits using precise quantifiers, and interviewers compare them to company expectations. Include a complication like a sudden deadline change.
rw: Read a short article on 'Digital Detox Habits', highlighting sentences with quantifiers. Then write a 120-word paragraph comparing your own habits to those in the article.
st: Read a short story about a Moroccan professional balancing work and family, using target language. Close with: 'Today we compared lifestyles with precise quantifiers—great work!'
g: Students bid on true/false habit statements using play money.
Pairs trade habits using 'I tend to...' and 'I hardly ever...'.
Students race to write sentences with 'plenty of' and 'hardly any' on the board.
Match professions to habit descriptions using quantifiers.
Act out a habit with a twist (e.g., 'hardly ever sleeping well' before a big event).
diff: Fast finishers: write a 150-word email to a friend comparing their lifestyles using target language.
Support learners: use a sentence frame worksheet to describe habits with quantifiers.
hw: Complete the 'Lifestyles and Habits' practice task from the library folder.
Interview a family member about their habits and write a 100-word summary.
Write a 120-word paragraph comparing your lifestyle to a friend's using quantifiers.
tip: Encourage students to relate habits to local contexts like Ramadan or family gatherings to make language relevant.
